answer: On average there are approximately 52 CHIP variants per sample (52.33) after filtering out intronic, intergenic, and UTR variants. Across the 86 samples, 11,896 raw variant rows (rows with Zygosity = Heterozygous or Homozygous Variant; 'Reference' and no-call rows excluded) reduced to 4,500 variants after dropping rows annotated as intron_variant, 3_prime_UTR_variant, 5_prime_UTR_variant, or 5_prime_UTR_premature_start_codon_gain_variant (no intergenic_variant rows exist). Per-sample counts range 39–66 with median 52. Sensitivity note: if splice_region_variant (2,664 rows; always a single-term annotation here) were also excluded, the average would be 47.24 (median 46.5).
